As NASA’s Voyager 1 crosses a full light-day away from Earth, it sits nearly twelve billion miles into deep space. But what if we could actually see a visible beam of light traveling that immense distance? Because space is a vacuum, a flash from our planet would remain invisible until it struck the spacecraft's copper antenna. At that extreme range, your flashlight beam would take twenty-four full hours just to deliver a single photon hello. Would you wave back at a probe you can't even see? Follow for more what-ifs.
